per_depth.common_affordance: The statement explicitly reduces every guaranteed-impossible instance to testing one-job duration and the two independent stage-load sums.
The statement directly enumerates the complete set of certificate conditions as simple inequalities on individual job totals and the two stage sums.
The statement exposes an exhaustive set of additive necessary conditions: an isolated job needs p1+p2 time, while a stage needs the sum of its processing times.
The certificate conditions are exactly independent arithmetic lower bounds: p1+p2>T for a job or the sum of one stage's durations>T, together with the promise that one such bound applies.
The explicit promise that every impossible instance has a JOB or LOAD certificate
The statement explicitly reduces certificate validity to checking whether one row sum or one column sum exceeds T.
The certificate definitions are separable: an isolated job is contradictory exactly when p1 + p2 > T, while an isolated stage is contradictory exactly when the sum of its processing times exceeds T.
The stated relaxations remove enough constraints that JOB feasibility becomes the single-team inequality p1+p2<=T and LOAD feasibility becomes the single-lane total-length inequality sum(lengths)<=T.

The relaxation rules eliminate all interactions except a single lane's total non-overlapping packing or a single team's sequential pair, so every scenario reduces directly to comparing additive lengths with T.
The rules reduce every isolated contradiction to zero-clearance one-dimensional packing: a pair fails exactly when p1+p2>T, and a lane fails exactly when the sum of its vehicle lengths exceeds T.
